## Key Tips for a Successful Second Half

Dear all,


I hope your exams went well, and I look forward to seeing you back in class!


As we continue with the Introduction to Programming, I want to highlight a few important points to help everyone succeed.


1. We have to keep moving forward as a class.


During lectures, I need to focus on teaching the material and making progress with the entire group. Unfortunately, we cannot spend extended periods debugging individual technical problems while everyone else is waiting.


I am happy to help before or after class, especially with issues related to setting up your working directory or development environment.


2. Make sure your technical setup works.


If you repeatedly encounter the same technical issues, please take responsibility for finding a sustainable solution. This might include using a different computer or considering an affordable (e.g., refurbished Windows) laptop suitable for the course.


Having a reliable working environment is essential for keeping up with the exercises.


3. Important: You MUST understand pandas!


In particular, make sure you understand how to access and select data in a DataFrame using:


- df.loc[] – label-based selection
- df.iloc[] – position-based selection


These are fundamental skills that we will continue to build on. Please practice them independently if you are not yet comfortable using them.


4. Come to class and participate!


I strongly encourage you to attend regularly. Those who show up, actively participate, and practice the exercises put themselves in the best position to pass the course. Consistency matters!


5. Your feedback matters.


I will continue using the surveys to understand what works well and what could improve your learning experience. If there is anything else I can do to support your learning, please let me know through the surveys.


My goal is for everyone to succeed, but we also need to keep progressing together. I am happy to support you, and I ask you to take an active role in your own learning.


Looking forward to seeing you in class!


Best regards,
Gerit Wagner
